bollymeter.basis: Kyoto Animation's visual peak: critics at ANN awarded an A grade for direction, music, and Violet's character arc from weapon to empathetic writer. IMDb audience scores it 8.4/10.

pull_quotes.text: From her own beginnings as a discarded tool to her final emergence as an abundantly compassionate hero, Violet is a terrific protagonist.

seasons.review_body: Violet Evergarden aired on Netflix from January 11 to April 5, 2018, produced by Kyoto Animation under director Taichi Ishidate. Anime News Network's Nick Creamer awarded the series an A grade, calling Violet a terrific protagonist whose arc from discarded weapon to compassionate Auto Memory Doll is rendered with exceptional craft. The IMDb audience rating of 8.4 from a substantial vote base confirms a near-consensus of excellence.

episode_reviews.title: I Love You
episode_reviews.review_body: Violet Evergarden Season 1 Episode 10 'I Love You' aired March 15, 2018 on Netflix. The series holds an IMDb audience rating of 8.4; ANN's Nick Creamer awarded the series an A grade. ANN's episode-specific review called this 'one of the best stories in the series, the best example of how letter-writing can change a person's life.' The episode became the series' most discussed hour online: a terminally ill mother asks Violet to write letters to her daughter for every birthday the child will have without her. The concept is simple; Kyoto Animation's execution is not. The episode's restraint - the letters never read aloud, the mother's voice unheard by the daughter, the grief communicated entirely through the daughter reading words written in her mother's absence - produced the scene that broke audiences worldwide and confirmed the series' standing as Kyoto Animation's character-craft peak. The 9.8 bollymeter is the series' highest individual episode score.

episode_reviews.title: The Day I Stopped Being a Tool
episode_reviews.review_body: Violet Evergarden Season 1 Episode 13 'The Day I Stopped Being a Tool' aired April 5, 2018 on Netflix as the series finale. The series holds an IMDb audience rating of 8.4; ANN's Nick Creamer awarded an A grade, describing Violet as a protagonist whose arc from discarded weapon to compassionate Auto Memory Doll is rendered with exceptional craft. The finale achieves the payoff the thirteen episodes built toward: Violet finally comprehending the words Major Gilbert said to her - the emotional content she spent a full season learning the vocabulary to receive. Kyoto Animation's direction reserves its most detailed and emotionally calibrated character work for the finale's key sequences. The 9.1 bollymeter is the second-highest individual episode score in the series, below only Episode 10's 9.8, reflecting a finale that earns its emotional resolution without diminishing the grief it took to get there.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode carries the highest individual episode score on IMDb among the finale batch, affirming that the series earned its emotional conclusion.
